title: Cap. II: fourth cause (cruelty charge); leave old Scholastics — Pontificii & Arminians next
pass_a_gloss: The last cause, by which very many have been moved to admit no election unless propped on foresight of some act to be elicited from the power of free choice, seems to me to have been this: That they presumed as a necessary postulate what is most false, namely, that God would be cruel unless he should set it in every man's power that he be able to recover by himself the salvation which he lost in Adam. But the old Pelagians and Scholastics being dismissed, let us join battle with those who in this our age disturb the Church, while they try to refresh old errors and thrust them in under new formulas of words. And first we will deal against certain Pontificals, then against the Arminians: who in this agree, that they admit no election unto salvation unless propped on foresight of human acts to be elicited, from free choice prevented by grace. Key lemmas: postulatum fallissimum; Deus crudelis; Pontificii; Arminiani; praescientia actuum; gratia praeveniens.
pass_b_english: A last motive for many who will admit no election except one resting on foresight of some act free choice can elicit: they took as a necessary postulate what is utterly false — that God would be cruel unless he put it in every person's power to recover by himself the salvation lost in Adam. Leave the old Pelagians and Scholastics. Engage those who disturb the Church in our age by dressing old errors in new formulas. First certain Papal doctors, then the Arminians: both refuse any election to salvation that does not rest on foresight of human acts elicited from free choice, grace having gone before.
source_text: Postrema causa, qua moti sunt quamplurimi ut nullam admitterent electionem, nisi praescientia nixam alicujus actus eliciendi ex potestate liberi arbitrii, hac mihi fuisse videtur, Quod tanquam necessarium postulatum praesumpserunt, quod est fallissimum, scilicet, Deum crudelem fore, nisi in cujusvis hominis potestate constituat ut salutem possit, quam in Adamo emisit, per seipsum recuperare. Sed missis veteribus Pelagianis & Scholasticis, congrediamur cum illis qui nostro hoc seculo perturbant Ecclesiam, dum veteres errores interpolare & sub novis verborum formulis obtrudere conantur. Atque primo agemus contra Pontificios quosdam, dein contra Arminianos: qui in hoc consentiunt, quod electionem nullam ad salutem admittunt nisi nixam praescientia actuum humanorum eliciendorum, ex libero arbitrio per gratiam praevento.
